chunks: Hammad narrated from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about the 'Ma'tuh' (one whose mind has wandered/insane), whether his divorce is valid? He said, "What is it?" I said, "The foolish one who has lost his mind." He said, "Yes."

And there is no contradiction between the first report and this, because we interpret his saying 'his divorce is valid' as meaning: if his guardian divorces her on his behalf, and he himself does not preside over it. What indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهِ: The Ma'tuh: a person with mild insanity or wandering mind, distinct from complete insanity

ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of an insane person (Ma'tuh) valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the legal status of the 'Ma'tuh' (one with mild insanity or wandering mind), confirming that their divorce is valid. The Imam’s brief response, coupled with the scholarly explanation, indicates that while the individual may lack full competence to initiate divorce themselves, the act is legally binding when performed by their guardian (wali), thereby resolving apparent contradictions in earlier reports.
